newsitem.title: USA: Stock market to eye earnings, economic data.
newsitem.headline: Stock market to eye earnings, economic data.

text.p: Wall Street stocks, struggling for their footing after a sharp pullback, will turn this week to a key piece of economic data and fourth-quarter earnings reports from companies including Coca-Cola Co. and Procter & Gamble Co.
Market watchers said that the downdraft in stocks that began with a 94-point Dow loss on Thursday is likely to carry through this week as investors take further profits from the New Year's rally.
"This market has been in a danger zone for the last five or six sessions," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
While saying the market's underlying fundamentals remained strong, Cardillo added, "I can see it going down a total of 5 percent."
The Dow Jones industrial average fell 59.27 points on Friday to 6,696.48, after a 94 point drop on Thursday, to end the week off 136.62 points, or 2 percent.
The blue chip index had risen over 7 percent in January through Thursday's intra-session high, before reversing its course.
A report on the fourth quarter Employee Cost Index, a barometer of how much companies pay for employees, will be closely watched by both stock and bond markets.
Analysts said a higher-than-expected ECI number could damage the inflation-sensitive bond market and rekindle fears of a Federal Reserve hike in interest rates.
"People are looking at that for (signs of) inflation pressure on wages," said Bruce Bittles, market strategist at J.C. Bradford.
Economists generally expect the ECI to rise 0.9 percent in the fourth quarter, compared with a 0.6 percent gain in the third quarter. The report is due ahead of the stock market's opening Tuesday.
Analysts said they will also be paying close attention to fourth-quarter profit reports from large consumer products companies such as Coke and Procter & Gamble.
Beyond the latest earnings, market players said they will also look for any indication from the companies that the recent strength in the dollar will hurt future profits.
While large-capitalisation stocks could be hurt by the effects of the strong dollar, small-cap shares, which have lagged the big names so far this year, may benefit, Bittles said.
Multi-nationals see their foreign earnings shaved by a strong dollar, while smaller companies can benefit by paying less in dollar terms for imported raw materials.
The Nasdaq Composite index down 14.54 points to 1,363.83. The index was up 14.78 on the week.

The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 7.04 to 770.52, leaving that index 5.65 points lower for the week. The American Stock Exchange index edged down 1.53 to 588.16, down 1.79 on the week.
